local_articles.title: McCullum stands down as England Test team head coach
local_articles.snippet: Brendon McCullum has left his role as England's Test head coach but will remain in charge of the national white-ball set-up, the England and Wales Cricket Board announced Sunday. England have lost seven of their last nine Tests under the former New Zealand captain. This includes a woeful 4-1 Ashes defeat in Australia in 2025/26 and last month's 2-1 loss at home to New Zealand, with both series overshadowed by allegations of a team drinking culture. "I've absolutely loved coaching the Test side and I'm incredibly proud of what we've achieved together," said McCullum in an ECB statement, adding: "Of course I'm gutted not to be continuing, but I respect the decision." questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.

Theresa Lazaro (May 6), Naypyitaw has granted zero access to any organization, while Lazaro's June 10 announcement of planned outreach to ethnic resistance organizations risks further junta resistance and no public movement exists on ICRC prison visits. With half of 2026 elapsed and over five years of unbroken refusal, 'No organization qualified' rises (0.35 to 0.44); among organizations, ASEAN (0.24 to 0.25, backed by an active formal Chair request and June 19 letter from 134 parliamentarians ahead of July's ASEAN meetings) moves ahead of ICRC (0.30 to 0.21), with UN trimmed (0.08 to 0.07) and WHO at 0.01.

local_articles.title: ASEAN hopes to see progress on peace plan by Myanmar
local_articles.snippet: BANGKOK – ASEAN hopes to see demonstrable progress from Myanmar on the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) peace plan, such as the release of all political detainees including Aung San Suu Kyi, Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said on July 12. “The most important point was that we all reaffirmed the central importance of the Five Point Consensus – it was and it remains valid. The next point is that all of us want to see demonstrable progress,” he told the Singapore media after an informal meeting between ASEAN foreign ministers and their Myanmar counterpart in Bangkok. It was the first in-person meeting between the ASEAN foreign ministers and Myanmar’s top diplomat since the 2021 coup in Myanmar. Balakrishnan also mentioned that ASEAN foreign ministers would like to see a permanent end to violence in Myanmar and for ASEAN to be able to deliver humanitarian aid across the country eve

local_articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi's health update from Myanmar
local_articles.snippet: BANGKOK - Foreign ministers from the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN were told on July 12 by their Myanmar counterpart that detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi is in good health and would be looked after, ASEAN’s special envoy to Myanmar said. Maria Theresa Lazaro, the Philippine Foreign Minister, has been seeking access to Suu Kyi, 81, who has been detained since her elected government was ousted in a 2021 military coup. “My recollection of the statement of the Myanmar Foreign Minister on Aung San Suu Kyi is that she’s in good health and that the premise of how he said this is that she is a relative, she’s a sister and therefore we will take care of her,” Lazaro told a press conference. questions.title: Who will win the main MotoGP race at the 2026 British Grand Prix?
questions.background: The main Grand Prix race is separate from the sprint race held during the same MotoGP weekend.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official MotoGP classification for the 2026 British Grand Prix main race at Silverstone. Resolution : Resolve to the rider declared the winner of the main race scheduled for August 9, 2026. The sprint race does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning rider's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-11 German GP Sachsenring injury and form evidence (MotoGP.com, Motorsport.com, Crash.net, The Race, Reuters): (1) Former Silverstone favorite and defending 2025 winner Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia)—already returning from an Assen concussion after three straight Sunday DNFs—suffered a 'complete and displaced fracture of the left clavicle' in a violent Q2 highside at Turn 7 and is flying back to Italy for July 12 surgery with Dr. Giuseppe Porcellini, missing the German GP. While MotoGP's four-week summer break gives him ~26 days before Silverstone FP1 (August 7) and Aprilia boss Paolo Bonora hopes he returns, combining DNS/complication risk (~10-15%), post-op upper-body fatigue over a 20-lap high-speed Silverstone GP, and severe recent crash/confidence form slashes Bezzecchi sharply (0.22 -> 0.13). (2) Healthy championship leader Jorge Martin (+11 over Bezzecchi before Sunday GP, Assen pole/P3 on Silverstone's closest analogue, P6 in Sachsenring Sprint) becomes clear Silverstone #1 favorite (0.20 -> 0.22). (3) Trackhouse Aprilia duo impressed even at tight anti-clockwise Sachsenring: Assen GP winner Ai Ogura finished P4 in the Sprint right behind the Ducati 1-2-3 (0.15 -> 0.17) and Assen Sprint winner/GP runner-up Raul Fernandez held provisional pole, qualified P4 (top Aprilia), and finished P5 in Sprint (0.09 -> 0.11). (4) Marc Marquez shattered the Sachsenring lap record (1:19.041) for pole and cruised to Sprint victory; though clockwise Silverstone strongly favors Aprilia (winless there since 2014), four weeks to hit 100% fitness plus Bezzecchi's injury lift Marquez (0.12 -> 0.14). Residual 23% preserves Silverstone's historic parity (11 different winners in last 11 editions), British rain, and surging Ducatis (Alex Marquez Sprint P2, Fabio Di Giannantonio Sprint P3, Bagnaia) plus Pedro Acosta.

questions.title: If Morgan Rogers leaves Aston Villa during the 2026 summer transfer window, which club will he join?
questions.background: Morgan Rogers is an England international and an attacking player for Aston Villa.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from either club confirming a completed permanent transfer, corroborated by reputable sports reporting. Resolution Conditions : Conditional on Rogers completing a permanent transfer away from Aston Villa during the 2026 summer transfer window, resolve to the acquiring club. If he completes multiple transfers during the window, use his first permanent transfer from Aston Villa. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the acquiring football club.

Enforcing strict anti-overconfidence calibration for an unconfirmed, pre-bid transfer rumor with a GBP 30m-50m valuation gap trims Arsenal from 0.65 -> 0.55, lifting Chelsea (0.15 -> 0.18), Liverpool (0.05 -> 0.08), and Manchester United (0.04 -> 0.07), holding Manchester City at 0.06 (after their GBP 116m Elliot Anderson signing), and leaving 6% residual for PSG/Real Madrid/Bayern/other.

questions.title: Which club will sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig in summer 2026?
questions.background: Yan Diomande is an Ivory Coast winger playing for RB Leipzig.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by RB Leipzig or the destination club confirming an agreement for Diomande's permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the destination club in the first such agreement announced between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the destination club.
questions.current_reasoning: July 6-9 reporting (AFP, L'Equipe, Abdellah Boulma, Liverpool.com, Anfield Watch) further solidifies Paris Saint-Germain's lead conditional on a permanent transfer, while showing club-to-club talks remain unconfirmed and complex. Diomande has reportedly agreed on a five-year contract with PSG; Liverpool cooled their interest after having a EUR 90m+10m bid rejected and Diomande choosing PSG (having already signed Victor Munoz and exploring alternative forwards); and on July 9 AFP confirmed PSG is actively holding talks with RB Leipzig for Diomande (and Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche) while freeing attacking slots and cash by selling Goncalo Ramos to AC Milan and finalizing Lee Kang-in's ~EUR 40m sale to Atletico Madrid. However, L'Equipe (July 7) and Boulma (July 8) caution that PSG are 'in no rush,' reluctant to meet Leipzig's EUR 120m-130m valuation (discussing player-plus-cash options), and could face a late hijack (like Tottenham's Xavi Simons hijack from Chelsea last summer) if negotiations deadlock. Accordingly, we nudge PSG up to 0.64 (0.60 -> 0.64, staying strictly below 0.65 before official club agreement), trim Liverpool (0.28 -> 0.23), and keep Chelsea (0.04), Real Madrid (0.03), and Bayern Munich (0.03, up from 0.02, explicitly named by RB chief Mintzlaff), leaving 3% tail.
